column1: # Coverage floors per package, read by covcheck (tools/build/coverage).
# <package> is a directory holding a BUCK file (src/<module>); the floors are
# basis points (1/100 of a percent, 0 to 10000, so 8734 is 87.34%); the
# branch floor is '-' when the package has none. A pinned row has a fourth
# field, its reason (never empty): floors set by hand under what was measured,
# for lines covered only on some runs; they are kept as written. Rows are sorted by package
# in byte order, each package once. A floor may only rise: covcheck reports a
# package measured below its floor, or a floor above 0 with nothing measured
# for it (Regression), a measured package with no row (MissingRow), a row whose directory has no BUCK file (ExtraRow) and a
# measured branch value whose row has '-' (BranchFloorMissing), and writes the
# file with every floor raised to what it measured (--ratchet-out) to copy in.
# A Regression fails the gate in every mode, census included, so the package's
# conda package is not built: coverage can only go up.
# The rows are the census's: census.sh render writes them from census.tsv,
# raising a floor to what was measured and never lowering one, and the build
# (//:coverage_census) holds them to it. A floor that must stay under the
# measurement is a pinned row here (census.md).
